<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **10** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/security.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via ObjectSchemaBase (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **10** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/security.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d83d4a340f61f41be45eb9f77575d2f2a8839771` — the merge of head `e254e52d0a9feea667b7b2d35caf7676e33e573b` into base `d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d83d4a340f61f41be45eb9f77575d2f2a8839771 && git checkout d83d4a340f61f41be45eb9f77575d2f2a8839771
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2 e254e52d0a9feea667b7b2d35caf7676e33e573b && git checkout -B drift-repro d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2 && git merge --no-ff e254e52d0a9feea667b7b2d35caf7676e33e573b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Both are this PR's own key, so they are this PR's to fix.
- **File surface extended by the seat (the claiming seat follows its own breakage):** `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts` and its test, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts`, and the changeset. No open PR touches these files, and no in-flight claim names them. Declared to the `domain:engine` seat on #6367.
- **What the push carries:**
  - the held patch: `defaultRowScope: ruleEntry` in `OBJECT_REFERENCE_POSITIONS` (one policy, dropped whole when it mentions a denied field, the `validations` posture), and the count 45 → 46 with its history sentence;
  - one pin beside it in `object-schema-fls-references.test.ts`, the way the file pins its other rule positions: an object whose `defaultRowScope.using` names a denied field is served without the key, and the control (no denied field named) keeps it unchanged;
  - `@objectstack/metadata-core` in the changeset, at the bump and in the form the repo's changeset gate takes. No behaviour moves until an object declares the key; say so there.
- **The PR body:** one combined set of `pr_body_edits`, written against the live body (still the round-0 text: the seat has not applied round 1's six pairs), covering rounds 1 and 2, with the downstream-importers section saying the two pins are fixed in this PR, not held.
- **Push once** after the fix and the pin are green locally: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-core test`, the meta-types file, `metadata-core` typecheck, and the gate re-derivation on the final head. CI is read on the new head.
- **After the push:** the seat checks the new head and runs the contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. `needs:contract-review` goes on the PR then. This is the last patch round before the review (the review-loop limit is two).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e254e52d0a9feea667b7b2d35caf7676e33e573b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/data/object-default-row-scope.test.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts, packages/spec/liveness/object.json, packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/object.md, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, packages/spec/src/compose-stacks-merge-config-object-refusal.test.ts, packages/spec/src/compose-stacks-merge-collection-refusal.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/security.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/security.json, packages/spec/authorable-defaults/security.json, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-org-axis-red-lines.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, .changeset/24338-object-default-row-scope.md

Inputs read: card #24338 (body and all five comments: the claim `6254274655`, the three dev reports, the file-surface extension `6255545754`), ruling E′ on #24164 (`6250748677`), the PR body and file list, the net diff of the head against the merge base `1eae21f9719db38bff33477f4613216c370554f1` (26 files, +549/−83; `git merge-base` confirms that base), the two riders this PR carried out (`6255156624` on #24341, `6255162631` on #24340), objectui at the console pin `0707b4ae37` (read-only), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only throughout: the head was fetched into a private ref, nothing was built, run or re-run; the record template was rendered with `record-recognisers --template --paths` over the PR's 26 paths, which returns the two `hits` above.

Check-runs on `e254e52d0`, read at 2026-10-18T22:22:00Z and again at 2026-10-18T22:27:44Z (50 runs): `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset` (three runs, all success, the last completing between the two reads), `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, every `Lint ·` leg, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, the claim and single-writer guards: success. Skipped by design: `Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance`, the dogfood shards, the packed-tarball smoke. Still in progress at the second read: `Test Core (1/6 … 6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace`. Final reading at 2026-10-18T22:49:44Z (52 runs, after polling every 30 seconds): every run completed, 42 success and 10 skipped, none failed. The five required contexts all conclude success: `Lint & Repo Gates` (22:19:52Z), `TypeScript Type Check` (22:33:00Z), `Build Core` (22:21:07Z), `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (22:16:08Z) and `Test Core` (22:49:31Z, all six shards green, including 5/6 and 6/6, the two that were red on the earlier heads `8964dfbbb` and `62170b56e` on exactly the two pins commit `91b2f39f3` fixes).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ObjectSchema` accept set widens by exactly one optional key, `defaultRowScope`.** Right. Additive: an object that parsed before parses unchanged and its parsed output carries no `defaultRowScope` (the control case in `object-default-row-scope.test.ts`). The key is reached at every door an object parse reaches because there is one declaration: the `object` metadata write door binds `ObjectSchema` (`kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts:91`), `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.objects` is `z.array(ObjectSchema)` (`stack.zod.ts:642`), so `defineStack` and `os validate` (`cli/src/commands/validate.ts:349`, `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse`) parse it too. The refusal of `object` is located: `strictObject` closes the shape (`z.object(shape, { error }).strict()`), the `unrecognized_keys` issue lands at path `defaultRowScope` with `keys: ['object']`, and `suggestions.zod.ts` answers an exact `guidance` entry with the prescription bullet and suppresses the rename channel, so the message carries "`object` is implied on a default row scope … Delete the key." Pinned on the authoring door and on the registry door.

2. **`DefaultRowScopeSchema` is the policy schema minus `object`, shared by reference.** Right, and the sharing is structural rather than textual: `members` is destructured from `RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema.shape` (same member instances, pinned with `toBe` per key), the cross-field rules are the one named function `refineRowLevelSecurityPolicy` (reads `operation`, `using`, `check`, never `object`), and the near-miss table is the one const `RLS_POLICY_ALIASES` (targets `positions`, `check`, `using`, all members of the scope). Members, rules and aliases cannot drift; only `surface`, `history` and the `object` guidance are the scope's own. Accept set, judged against the policy: the policy requires `object`, the scope refuses it; every other value the policy accepts the scope accepts, with the same `enabled: true` default and the same two refusals (no clause: `custom` at `defaultRowScope`; `check` on `select`: `custom` at `defaultRowScope.check`). The two tombstones `priority` and `tags` are `retiredKey()` = `z.never().optional()`, which accepts only absence, so leaving them out changes nothing either schema accepts; the one difference is the refusal text (the policy answers with the upgrade prescription for `rowLevelSecurity[]`, the scope answers as an unknown key), which is the right text for a surface that never had the key. The compile-time pin holds the input type equal to the policy input type with `object`, `priority` and `tags` omitted. The zod 4 `.omit()` refusal on a refined object schema is real (the policy schema carries `.superRefine`), so rebuilding from shared parts is the sound route, not a workaround.

3. **`RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema`'s contract did not move.** Right. The removed inline `.superRefine` body and the added function body carry the same two issues, the same messages and the same `check` path; the alias object moved verbatim into the const. Its rows in `authorable-surface/security.json`, `authorable-defaults/security.json`, `api-surface/security.json`, the `security/RowLevelSecurityPolicy` entry in `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` and its generated `rls.mdx` table are untouched by the diff; the diff to those shards is only the `DefaultRowScope` additions. The claim's "no change to `RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema` itself" is met as a contract statement, and the source restructure is declared in the PR body and the round-0 report as a deviation rather than slipped in.

4. **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec/security` gains three exports** (`DefaultRowScopeSchema`, `DefaultRowScope`, `DefaultRowScopeParsed`), one JSON Schema (`security/DefaultRowScope`), eight authorable rows and one default row. Right: all additive, each shard moved by its generator, `declaration-map` and `export-origins` consistent with the source file.

5. **`composeStacks` with `objectConflict: 'merge'` now refuses two stacks declaring a different `defaultRowScope`.** Right, and it is new-key behaviour only. The refusal set is derived from `ObjectSchema.shape` at first use (`objectUnmergeableKeys()` in `stack.zod.ts`, `declaresConfigObject` on an optional fixed-shape object); the composer is not in the diff. Nothing that composes today narrows: `git grep defaultRowScope` on the head outside `packages/spec` finds only the changeset, the generated reference pages carrying the describe, the metadata-core classification and its pin, and the meta-types count's history sentence; no stack, no object, no example declares the key, and objectui at the pin has zero hits. The two literal pins gained the key in shape order.

6. **`@objectstack/metadata-core`: `defaultRowScope: ruleEntry` in `OBJECT_REFERENCE_POSITIONS`.** Right posture. `ruleEntry` is the per-entry test `ruleEntries` already applies to `validations` (`mentionsDenied(entry, denied, 'include', 'classified')`): the scope is one CEL rule over this object's record whose prose describes the field, and the mask is a served-document projection, never enforcement. Dropping the policy whole is correct next to `validations`: scrubbing only `using` would serve a policy with no predicate, which reads as restricting nothing and would not re-parse (the refinement requires `using` or `check`). The pin's third leg does separate the classification from the unclassified fail-safe: in `mentionsDenied`, the `'all'` reading walks with `testKeys = true` and tests every object key with `stringMentions(key, denied)`, so a denied field named `operation` drops the scope on the fail-safe path, while the `'classified'` reading walks with `testKeys = false` and never tests keys, so the scope survives. The dev's ablation measured exactly that (two legs: coverage test alone red; three legs: pin and coverage test red). Without the classification the coverage test `classify each new ObjectSchema key in OBJECT_REFERENCE_POSITIONS` is red, which is what turned `Test Core` red on the two earlier heads and is fixed on this one.

7. **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: the served `object` property count moves 45 to 46.** Right: a test-only change with its history sentence, no published source moved, no changeset owed.

8. **Liveness ledger.** Right. `defaultRowScope` is `planned` with `authorWarn` and an `authorHint`, drilled into eight `planned` children (the gate refuses an undeclared container and would refuse a deferral to `permission/rowLevelSecurity` whose key set differs), only the container warns, and the note states the flip condition in the `action.outcomeMessages` spelling: `live` on the commit that lands #24340, citing `collectRLSPolicies`, dropping `authorWarn` / `authorHint` in the same edit. State counts 0 to 8 planned, 54 to 62 classified. `Spec property liveness`: success.

9. **Studio form.** Right. The root-path `omit` row for `object.defaultRowScope` records a `why` that is exactly Prime Directive #10: a form row would let an author declare a row restriction that filters nothing, and the writers are to be code-declared platform objects, none of which declares it yet.

10. **`dropped-refinements.baseline.json`.** Right. One new root entry `security/DefaultRowScope` plus the `defaultRowScope` site under each of the nine `ObjectSchema` embeddings (`data/Object`, three `system/*` change-set shapes, five `api/*` responses): 240/781 from 239/771 is one schema and ten sites, which is 1 + 9. The refinement is the policy's own and has no JSON Schema form, exactly as `security/RowLevelSecurityPolicy`, already listed.

11. **Prime Directive #10, the claim as narrow as the enforcement.** Holds. The published describe states every semantic as a contract to be met ("is to apply", "is to be used as authored", "is to be unaffected"), names the writers as "are to declare", and says once, plainly: "Not applied yet: no server reads this key in this release, so declaring it filters no rows." The changeset says "What it does today: nothing." The `authorHint` says "Not applied yet". The form `why` says "none declares it yet". The TSDoc on `DefaultRowScopeSchema` says "Neither exists yet". The clause "the one step every read, write and explain passes through" is a claim about today's tree and is consistent with ruling item 2's naming of `collectRLSPolicies` in `security-plugin.ts`, which exists with call sites on the read, write-check and explain paths.
